title: SARS-CoV-2 spike protein unlikely to bind to integrins via the Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) motif of the Receptor Binding Domain: evidence from structural analysis and microscale accelerated molecular dynamics
authors: Houcemeddine Othman; Haifa Ben Messaoud; Oussema Khamessi; Hazem Ben Mabrouk; Kais Ghedira; Avani Bharuthram; Florette Treurnicht; Ikechukwu Achilonu; Yasien Sayed; Najet Srairi-Abid
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学、对接和自由能景观分析SARS-CoV-2 RBD的RGD基序与整合素的结合可能性，属于蛋白质-蛋白质互作而非TF-DNA体系，但方法（MD、对接）可迁移至蛋白质-DNA互作建模，故给予中档评分。
abstract: The Receptor Binding Domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 virus harbors a sequence of Arg-Gly-Asp tripeptide named RGD motif, which has also been identified in extracellular matrix proteins that bind integrins as well as other disintegrins and viruses. Accordingly, integrins have been proposed as host receptors for SARS-CoV-2. The hypothesis was supported by sequence and structural analysis. However, given that the microenvironment of the RGD motif imposes structural hindrance to the protein-protein association, the validity of this hypothesis is still uncertain. Here, we used normal mode analysis, accelerated molecular dynamics microscale simulation, and protein-protein docking to investigate the putative role of RGD motif of SARS-CoV-2 RBD for interacting with integrins. We found, by molecular dynamics, that neither RGD motif nore its microenvironment show any significant conformational shift in the RBD structure. Highly populated clusters were used to run a protein-protein docking against three RGD-binding integrin types, showing no capability of the RBD domain to interact with the RGD binding site. Moreover, the free energy landscape revealed that the RGD conformation within RBD could not acquire an optimal geometry to allow the interaction with integrins. Our results highlighted different structural features of the RGD motif that may prevent its involvement in the interaction with integrins. We, therefore, suggest, in the case where integrins are confirmed to be the direct host receptors for SARS-CoV-2, a possible involvement of other residues to stabilize the interaction.
abstract_zh: SARS-CoV-2病毒的受体结合域（Receptor Binding Domain, RBD）含有一段名为RGD基序的Arg-Gly-Asp三肽序列，该序列也已在细胞外基质蛋白中被识别，这些蛋白与整合素（integrins）以及其他去整合素（disintegrins）和病毒结合。因此，整合素已被提议作为SARS-CoV-2的宿主受体。该假设得到了序列和结构分析的支持。然而，鉴于RGD基序的微环境对蛋白质-蛋白质结合施加了结构阻碍，该假设的有效性仍不确定。在此，我们使用简正模式分析（normal mode analysis）、加速分子动力学（accelerated molecular dynamics）微尺度模拟以及蛋白质-蛋白质对接，来研究SARS-CoV-2 RBD的RGD基序在与整合素相互作用中的假定作用。通过分子动力学，我们发现RGD基序及其微环境在RBD结构中均未显示出任何显著的构象变化。我们使用高居群聚类对三种RGD结合型整合素进行蛋白质-蛋白质对接，结果显示RBD结构域不具备与RGD结合位点相互作用的能力。此外，自由能景观揭示，RBD内的RGD构象无法获得允许与整合素相互作用的优化几何结构。我们的结果突出了RGD基序的不同结构特征，这些特征可能阻止其参与与整合素的相互作用。因此，我们建议，在整合素被确认为SARS-CoV-2直接宿主受体的情况下，其他残基可能参与以稳定该相互作用。
